title: Purposivism and fidelity to legislative purpose
shortTitle: Purposivism and fidelity to legislative purpose
summary: Purposivism interprets statutory language in light of the purposes attributed to the enacted legislation.
notes:
Identify the problem Congress addressed, the means it enacted, and the level of generality at which a claimed purpose operates. Katzmann’s version generally respects unambiguous text and uses reliable context to resolve uncertainty. The Hart-and-Sacks account limits interpretation to meanings the words can bear and recognizes clear-statement rules.

Holy Trinity is the source’s historical example of purpose narrowing broad coverage. Raila tests a proposed reading against the tort statute’s purposes and neighboring provisions. The Murphy litigation shows a disagreement about whether expert-fee reimbursement implements Congress’s intended scheme or exceeds the enacted authorization. A broad policy goal alone does not answer how Congress resolved a particular compromise, and the reading expressly acknowledges difficulty identifying a single purpose.
